note: P4380 (Pro 30:32) — if you have been foolish, exalting yourself, or devising evil, put your hand on your mouth.

dims.v: proud folly — vaunting oneself, to be stopped with silence
the folly of exalting oneself — the proud, foolish self-vaunting that, once recognised, calls for a hand clapped over the mouth, silence to halt the boasting before it does more harm
the evil-devising it is paired with (267251)
welded to the scheming of evil it is set beside

nabal (be foolish) — 'if you have been FOOLISH, exalting yourself... put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); proud self-exaltation is folly to be stopped by silence. When caught vaunting oneself, the wise course is to shut the mouth (cf 17:28).
malicious scheming — plotting evil, to be halted by silence
the devising of evil — the malicious plotting that, like proud folly, should be halted by clapping a hand over the mouth, stopping the scheme before it becomes speech and deed
the self-exalting folly it is paired with (267248)
welded to the proud folly it is set beside

zamam (devise/plot) — 'or if you have been DEVISING evil, put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); malicious scheming, like proud folly, is to be checked by silence — stop the plot before it hatches. Restraint of mouth restrains the evil (cf 30:33).
